acquisition: A serum-based 2D LC-MS assay using Parallel Reaction Monitoring is applied to quantify both calcyclin and heat shock protein 90.
PRM measurements were carried out on a nano-LC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Germering, Germany) online coupled to an Orbitrap Fusion mass spectrometer
targeted MS/MS mode set up as follows was used: isolation width 1.4 Da, HCD fragmentation
labeling: All digested sera were spiked with 40 fmol of both S100A6 and HSP90 stable isotope-labeled (SIL) peptides
quantification: A PRM assay was developed for quantitative measurements of S100A6 and HSP90 levels in serum using SIL peptides serving as internal standards
ratios between endogenous and SIL peptides of S100A6 and HSP90 were calculated to determine the concentrations
enrichment: Subsequently digested samples were fractionated by SCX chromatography to measure relatively low levels (ng mL-1) of S100A6 and HSP90 in sera
workflow_hints: PRM in Serum and Placental Tissue

primary_biological_variables.matched_definition: Comparison between diseased and healthy or unaffected controls.
evidence: Maternal serum levels of calcyclin and heat shock protein 90 are compared throughout pregnancy from the first trimester till term among women with preeclampsia (n = 43) and age‐matched normotensive pregnant controls (n = 46).
A case‐control study was conducted at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of the Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

Maternal serum levels of calcyclin and heat shock protein 90 are compared throughout pregnancy from the first trimester till term among women with preeclampsia (n = 43) and age‐matched normotensive pregnant controls (n = 46).
Sixty‐three percent of the samples were collected in the first trimester (<14 weeks), 17 percent in the second trimester (14–27 weeks) and 20 percent in the third trimester (≥28 weeks) of pregnancy.

replicate_hints: three technical (three PRM measurements of an identical sample (quality control) throughout the assay run) and three methodological (three independently prepared replicates of an SCX‐fractionated serum sample) replicates were measured
evidence: Maternal serum levels of calcyclin and heat shock protein 90 are compared throughout pregnancy from the first trimester till term among women with preeclampsia (n = 43) and age‐matched normotensive pregnant controls (n = 46).
Cases and controls were matched for maternal age, geographic origin, parity and gestational age at sampling.
Serum levels of calcyclin are significantly lower in patients with preeclampsia in the second trimester of pregnancy as compared to controls (p < 0.05).
Serum levels of heat shock protein 90 are significantly higher in patients with preeclampsia in the third trimester as compared to controls (p < 0.001).
